card.statement:
A formal distribution is an expression of the form

$$
a(z,w,\dots)=\sum_{m_1,m_2,\dots\in\mathbb Z}a_{m_1,m_2,\dots}z^{m_1}w^{m_2}\dots
$$

where the $a_{m_1,m_2,\dots}$ lie in some fixed vector space $V$.

If $A(z)$ is a field, then we set

\begin{equation}
A(z)_-:=\sum_{m\geq 0}A_{m}z^{-m-1},\quad\text{and}\quad
A(z)_+:=\sum_{m<0}A_{m}z^{-m-1}.
\end{equation}

The normal ordered product of two formal distributions $A(z)$ and $B(w)$ is defined by

$$
:A(z)B(w):=\displaystyle\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}\displaystyle\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}:A_mB_n:z^{-m-1}w^{-n-1}=A(z)_+B(w)+B(w)A(z)_-.
$$
card.label: Definition 1

paper.title: Virasoro action on Imaginary Verma modules and the operator form of the KZ-equation
paper.abstract: We define the Virasoro algebra action on imaginary Verma modules for affine sl(2) and construct the analogs of Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equation in the operator form. Both these results are based on a free field realization of imaginary Verma modules.
